Both halves resolved 2026-08-23; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md carries the evidence.

THE BIAS HALF IS REFUTED, by the arm built to test it. The claim was that denergy26 carries the filter to the first power and denergy27 carries it squared, so 26-27 could not vanish under a nontrivial filter however well the core conserves. With the filter OFF, f = 1, both terms carry the same weight by construction and the bias term is exactly zero -- and the residual is the LARGEST of the whole grid, 0.5575 against 0.1204 for kappa 8 at the same step. Removing the bias raises the residual 4.6x where the hypothesis needs it to fall to zero. Confirmed across nine further cells: the residual grows monotonically as the filter weakens at every timestep.

What the dependences say instead is truncation error. It scales with the timestep, ratios of 0.60 at dt 30 and 0.38-0.41 at dt 22.5 against linear's 0.667 and 0.500, consistent across kappa 8, 4 and 2. So water-and-energy-closure.md's attribution to the semi-implicit step stands, and its number is not a constant of the model: 0.31 W/m2 is what this timestep and this filter cost. Eight-orbit arms confirm the short windows to within 2%.

THE UNBOOKED HALF IS BOUNDED, by an identity that runs the wrong way for it. Nothing books the filter's KE removal -- mkdheat covers Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion, fluxmod the surface and vertical-diffusion terms, neither knows the filter exists -- and the filter preserves n=0 exactly so only the quadratic quantity is exposed. The kinetic-energy steady-state identity is what would find it, and a stronger filter removes more, so the gap must WIDEN with kappa if the filter is the missing term. It NARROWS: -0.013 to -0.000 at kappa 8, rising through +0.007 at kappa 2 to +0.039 with the filter OFF, where the filter's dissipation is identically zero and there is nothing to book.

At the adopted kappa 8 the identity closes to within 0.013 W/m2 against a conversion of about 2.1, six tenths of a percent. The term is real in principle and below what this instrument can see at production settings, so the row closes on the bound rather than on an mkdheat implementation.

REOPEN IF: the identity stops closing at the adopted kappa, or a rung's KE conversion grows enough that six tenths of a percent is worth chasing.

zcvel and the pit-filling increment were parameter(4.2) and a literal 1.0 in two copies, landmod's roffini and glaciermod's oroini, of which oroini is the one that survives. Both now derive from landmod_nl keys: zcvel = roffvel*ga**(0.5-roffexp) and zoroinc = roffpit*ga. Because zoro is geopotential, that makes the velocity proportional to sqrt(ga) once the slope is divided back to a topographic one, which is the open-channel scaling; the exponent is written as (0.5-roffexp) so the two cannot drift apart. roffvel = 2.022845 reproduces 4.200 at ga = 9.80665, and roffpit = 0.101972 m reproduces 1.000 m2/s2, so an Earth configuration is unchanged -- an identity that can fail. At this planet's gravity the effective zcvel is 4.575, 1.0893x upstream's, which is the 1.14x from sqrt(g) less the 1.049x the geopotential slope was already supplying.

Both densities are DECLARED AS INHERITED with the bracket reported, which is the second arm of the acceptance criterion. rhosnow joins landmod_nl and rhoglac joins glacier_nl, values unchanged at 330 and 850 kg/m3, so the bracket can now be RUN rather than only stated. The declaration beside each says what the constant does -- rhosnow converts water equivalent to the physical snow thickness that insulates the soil column, rhoglac to the ice thickness that enters the orography -- and that both are settled densities set by overburden compaction, which scales with gravity, so both are low on a planet whose surface gravity is 1.306x the one they were measured on. Not rescaled: firn densification is not a closed-form function of gravity that can be evaluated here, and this project brackets an estimate it cannot verify rather than guessing it. The bracket is the issue's own, roughly 10 to 20 per cent on snow insulation thickness and on glacier relief. glaciermod already had the GRAVITY right in the orography conversion, with its own comment; the density beside it is the half that is inherited, and that is now said where the two meet.

zh0 is now icemod_nl's HLEAD, declared in config at ExoPlaSim's value: exposed, not changed, and it reproduces the compiled 0.5 exactly. The thickness limit's melt is paid out of the same cell's conductive flux to the ocean instead of a global area-weighted sum spread over every other cell with ice below the limit; the old form was a heat transport with no carrier and it also dropped the remainder silently whenever demand exceeded capacity, since xcfluxr is reset at the top of every icestep. xmaxd is DECLARED OFF (-1.0) in config/planet.yaml and written to the namelist, so the branch cannot fire in any arm. The baseline climatology's bottom two sigma levels are 0.98282 and 0.92191; through the hypsometric relation at this world's gravity and a 280 K near-surface temperature that is a lowest full level near 110 m and a second near 510 m, so two levels below a kilometre and one below half. A Bodele-class nocturnal inversion and the jet core above it both fall inside the single lowest layer, whose wind is that layer's mean. The obstacle is not that the jet is weakly resolved, it is that the model has no interior to the layer the jet lives in, so no amount of high-cadence sampling recovers it.

It measures nitrification against soil WATER POTENTIAL in a silt loam, in two treatments that separate the two mechanisms -- shaken slurries with NH4 in excess, so only cell dehydration acts, fitting k = 15.4*exp(0.58*psi) with r2 0.958, and moist soil, where substrate diffusion acts too.

The bucket floor in landmod's land water step is unreachable in exact arithmetic: fluxmod's humidity solve takes AMAX1 against the level humidity so the surface evaporation never adds water, the line below it caps that same withdrawal at the store divided by the timestep on every land cell whatever the snowpack holds, and every other contribution to the surface flux adds because rainmod builds the snowfall rate as a subset of the total precipitation rate. The snow-exhaustion path this issue named is the wrong suspect: the cap is unconditional, so a snowpack absorbs part of a withdrawal already limited against the soil store and leaves the store fuller than bare ground would, not emptier. THE RATE LAW THE WHOLE ROW RESTED ON IS REFUTED. legmod.f90 folds the filter into every per-mode transform WEIGHT, and what passes through those weights is the nonlinear TENDENCY -- no filtered value is ever stored back into the prognostic spectral state. So the filter attenuates the source that fills a wavenumber by a fixed factor rather than damping the state at a rate, and its spectral effect carries no timestep. Two pairs differing in MPSTEP alone, same binary by sha, same cold start, same seed:

  T21 gamma 16, dt 45 -> 22.5: depth at 0.8N moves +0.009 dex, 0.1 sigma; rate law predicts -0.296 against a three-sigma bar of 0.15
  T42 gamma 16, dt 45 -> 30:   depth moves -0.007 dex, 0.2 sigma; predicted -0.169 against a bar of 0.08

The bite point does not move at either rung. So '2*kappa*(n/N)^gamma/dt, an e-folding every 169 seconds at the truncation, 450x to 1600x the hyperdiffusion' is not a rate the spectrum obeys, and the comparison it licensed is between a rate on the state and a thing that is not one.

THE SURVIVING LAW, exp(-2 kappa x^gamma), is confirmed on the gamma pair: T42 dt 30, gamma 8 vs 16, differing in NFILTEREXP alone, 12 two-orbit windows each. Depth at 0.8N moves +0.789 +/- 0.036 dex at 22 sigma where f^2 predicts +0.970 and the rate law +0.763; the sharper test is the gamma 8 bite point, where the two laws disagree by nearly a factor of two -- f^2 says 0.675, the rate law says 0.381, it measures 0.688.

WHAT KAPPA COSTS, measured. The whole of kappa 8 is worth 0.196 dex of depletion at 0.8 of the truncation, against a total measured depletion of 0.602 dex at T42 and 0.969 to 1.418 at T21. So the filter is a third of it at T42 and a fifth at T21; the hyperdiffusion and the spectrum's own steepening carry the rest, and world-ba0 measures the hyperdiffusion's share at 0.449 dex.

WHY NO KAPPA SWEEP WAS RUN. The confinement criterion goes as kappa^(-1/gamma) = kappa^(-1/16), so a factor of two in kappa moves the bite point by 0.030 of the truncation -- below the instrument's quantisation at T21 (1/21 = 0.048) and at it at T42 (1/42 = 0.024) against a measured three-sigma bar of 0.000 to 0.021. The acceptance criterion 'a kappa chosen against the spectral confinement criterion at each rung' is not achievable at the gamma the model runs. The depth at 0.8N can see a factor of two, at about 1.5 bars at T42 and below the bar at T21 -- so a sweep would price kappa, not choose it, and the price is already known analytically from a law now checked on two independent contrasts.
